rules.statement: The project-level build-scroll-3d-product-story skill must treat model inspection as a prerequisite and then enforce case research, multiple creative routes, an authored five-shot script, an animatic, explicit narrative confirmation, and only then runtime implementation.
Creative development must record applicable advertising references with source URLs, narrative theses, transferable methods, and model-specific limitations before a route is selected.
Creative development must compare at least two materially different routes and record the selected route; a generated explode-and-assemble preset is not a creative route.

The selected route must be expressed as exactly five continuous shots, each with a narrative purpose, viewer takeaway, action, camera, lighting, layout, transition, rhythm, hold, copy, and truth constraints.
A reviewable animatic with a fixed duration and evidence of review must exist after the five-shot script and before narrative confirmation or runtime manifest generation.
Narrative confirmation must identify the confirming person or role and durable evidence; the implementing agent must not self-approve its own route, script, or animatic.
Runtime-story generation and implementation instructions must fail closed when the ordered creative-development record is missing, incomplete, unapproved, or inconsistent with the selected route.
Research, scripts, and animation must stay within model and product evidence, record prohibited claims, and avoid inventing engineering function, assembly order, or product facts.

After narrative confirmation, keep product-specific choreography and content in approved artifacts while preserving a generic deterministic, reversible, demand-rendered runtime with poster and reduced-motion fallbacks.
Measure asset transfer and browser frame behavior only after the approved narrative is implemented; performance optimization must not substitute for or silently alter the confirmed shot intent.
